name: Productivity
tagline: 60 days to beat procrastination and build deep focus.
description: A neuroscience-based 60-day program to defeat procrastination and distraction — rewire the avoidance loop, train deep-focus attention, and build a daily execution system that compounds.

phases.label: P1
phases.title: Breaking the Cycle
phases.vibe: Procrastination is an emotional-avoidance loop: task → discomfort → escape to your phone → relief. The first two weeks break it by shrinking tasks until starting is easy and removing the escape hatches around you.

phases.label: P2
phases.title: Rewiring the Brain
phases.vibe: You still feel the pull to bail when work gets hard — now you have a routine for it. Time-block, single-task, and ride the discomfort for a few minutes until focus kicks in. Each rep strengthens your attention.

phases.label: P3
phases.title: Building a New Identity
phases.vibe: Deep work, follow-through, and calm focus are simply who you are now. You protect your peak hours, finish what you start, and build a system that compounds long past day 60.

0.title: Plan the day — pick 1 priority
0.note: Water, then write your single most important task (MIT). Deciding in advance removes the morning decision fatigue that fuels procrastination.

0.title: The 2-minute start
0.note: Commit to just 2 minutes on the hardest task. Starting — not finishing — is the barrier; motion creates motivation, not the reverse.

0.title: One 45-min focus block
0.note: Phone away, one task, timer on. Single-tasking rebuilds the focus circuits that constant switching degrades.

0.title: Remove one distraction
0.note: Silence the phone, close tabs, block a site. You can't out-willpower a slot machine — remove the cue instead.

0.title: 20 min movement
0.note: A walk or workout mid-day. Exercise boosts dopamine and focus and clears the mental fog that invites escape.

0.title: Pause before you bail
0.note: When you feel the urge to escape a task, breathe and name the feeling. Avoidance is emotional; labeling it hands control back to the thinking brain.

0.title: Shutdown review + plan tomorrow
0.note: List what you shipped and set tomorrow's MIT. A clear endpoint prevents work bleeding into rest and rumination.

0.title: Protect sleep 7-9 hrs
0.note: Sleep is the ultimate cognitive enhancer — willpower and focus collapse without it.

1.title: Plan + top 3 tasks
1.note: Set your MIT plus two supporting tasks. A short, ranked list beats an overwhelming one.

1.title: Two 50-min deep-work blocks
1.note: Two focused sprints with a break between. Building block length grows your attention capacity.

1.title: Run your anti-distraction routine
1.note: At your usual slump time, do the swap: stand, breathe, refocus — instead of grabbing the phone. Same cue, new routine.

1.title: 30 min movement
1.note: Exercise sharpens executive function for hours. Treat it as focus fuel, not a reward.

1.title: Single-task everything today
1.note: No multitasking. Task-switching has a real cognitive cost; doing one thing fully is faster and calmer.

1.title: Share progress / accountability
1.note: Tell someone what you'll finish today. Accountability harnesses social reward to drive follow-through.

1.title: Shutdown review
1.note: Close the loop, plan tomorrow. Reflection turns effort into a repeatable system.

2.title: Plan — automatic now
2.note: MIT set before the day starts. Systems, not willpower, run your days.

2.title: Deep work — your standard
2.note: Long, protected focus is who you are. Guard your peak hours ruthlessly.

2.title: Train — your standard now
2.note: Movement keeps the mind sharp and the mood steady.

2.title: Advance your biggest project
2.note: Pour compounding energy into the thing that matters most. Momentum is your identity now.

2.title: Weekly review of systems
2.note: Refine what works, cut what doesn't. Continuous improvement is the productivity edge.

2.title: Identity journal
2.note: Write as a disciplined person who finishes. Self-image drives daily action.

quotes: Starting is the whole battle. Motion makes motivation.
You don't need to feel like it. You need to begin.
Focus is a muscle — every block makes it stronger.
Procrastination is avoidance of a feeling, not a task.
Protect your peak hours like your life depends on it.
One deep-work block a day compounds into a different life.
Distraction is a choice you can stop making.
Discipline is choosing what you want most over what you want now.
Sixty days of showing up rewires who you are.
